newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bourse trades past $10 bln in January.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bourse trades past $10 bln in January.

text.p: Transactions on the Stock Exchange of Singapore (SES) crossed the Singapore $10 billion mark in January, the Straits Times newspaper said on Monday.
Transactions totalled $10.388 billion -- $9.9 billion on the mainboard and Clob International or over-the-counter trades, and $488.7 million on Sesdaq, the junior board -- the daily said.
The combined value of trades on the mainboard and Clob international was more than double December's $4 billion.

The overall performance was boosted by frenetic activity on Sesdaq where turnover on the junior board totalled 639.3 million shares valued at $488.7 million - a 57 percent year-on-year increase in volume and a 27 percent rise in value terms.
"Foreign currency-denominated issues continued to attract investors' interest as 359.3 million shares worth $869 million were traded last month, up 12 percent from December," the daily said.

It said the performance was similar to that at the begining of last year when trading was propped up mainly by what brokers dubbed the "January effect," with the bourse benefitting from high liquidity sparked by the return of foreign funds after the holiday season.

It said the launch of seven initial public offerings (IPOs) last month helped boost activity as the new issues saw 459.6 million shares traded, accounting for 10 percent of trading on the bourse last month.
It quoted Lum Chang Securities research manager Siow Sok Chuang as saying that the IPO phenomenon was likely to continue for the next few issues if they were fairly priced.

She said that institutional investors would wait and see if the next crop of corporate results due next month confirmed their earnings outlook for listed companies before investing any further in the stock market, the daily said.
